book.title: The Penguin Book of Independent Crosswords, volume 1

definitions.meaning: first meaning: get up onto one's feet
second meaning: hold good when tested, as an argument does

explanation.surface: A soldier gets to his feet for inspection on the parade ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one action, rising for an inspection; the two halves are separate senses of one phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both getting upright from sitting and surviving scrutiny, as a claim that holds up under examination.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a distinct section of society or the economy
second meaning: the wedge between two radii and an arc

explanation.walkthrough: Two plain meanings joined by 'or': a section of the economy, like the public one, and a pie-slice shape in geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a distinct area of activity or social group and a wedge-shaped region of a circle in geometry.

parts.note: surface reading: a skyscraper headquarters or a giant of business
setter's reading: industry is hard work, proverbially that of the busy insect, whose heaped nest rises like a tower

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower of industry' sounds like a business titan or a factory chimney; the industrious creatures here are insects building their mound.
explanation.definitionFit: The mound of earth thrown up by a busy insect colony is a small tower built by notably hard-working creatures.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Black Friar of the order founded by St Dominic
second meaning: belonging to Dominica or the ... Republic

explanation.surface: A monk who hails from the West Indies.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the pun: the friar is not from the Caribbean, the second sense is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a member of the preaching order of St Dominic and a native of the Dominican Republic or Dominica.

indicators.note: doing something carefully means crafting it, so these letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Who takes care to craft a witty comment? The answer names him.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: someone who shapes remarks with care is a coiner of phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasemaker is a person who coins striking expressions, which means crafting what is said with deliberate care.

clue.text: Ban English doctor on old ship

parts.note: standard abbreviation for English
Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek legend

explanation.surface: An English medic is barred from sailing on a historic vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is the usual crossword doctor alongside DR, MO and GP.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition, typically stopping trade or shipping with a particular country.

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so it is taken out of the word that follows

parts.note: a large Spanish sailing ship
gall is bile, and so resentment

explanation.surface: Lasting resentment drives someone to quit their vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: GALL leaves GALLEON, and what remains is the age.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immeasurably long period, an age, so it fits a long term of time.

parts.note: standard abbreviation for book
soft and floppy

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a conservative's book as feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp, a 1930s cartoon character, became the British byword for a pompous, reactionary old buffer.
explanation.definitionFit: From David Low's cartoon colonel, the name is used for any pompous person with diehard conservative views.

clue.text: Leave a note to indicate no change

parts.note: a break or time off work
taken as written
the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a memo saying nothing has changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' reads as a verb; it is the noun, a rest or holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate is to say the same thing again, confirming that the position or claim is unchanged.

parts.note: plain to see, open
a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: The point where a flat landscape and its stream start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like flat land; it is the adjective meaning obvious. The Ure is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is an opening, either a musical introduction or an initial approach in negotiations.

indicators.note: one thing set round another encloses it, so the vessel wraps the following words

parts.note: a can is a container or vessel
taken as written
the river dividing Devon from Cornwall

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a boat is to be found on some river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' does double duty: the whole clue describes a twin-hulled boat you might see on a river. The Tamar divides Devon from Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a sailing boat with two parallel hulls, a vessel that could well be seen on a river.

clue.text: Utter fabrication for which one has no time

indicators.text: for which one has no time
indicators.note: having no time means the abbreviation for time must be dropped from the word

parts.note: as in a tissue of lies, a fabrication
standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a total invention they have no patience for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective intensifying fabrication, but it is the verb, the definition; TISSUE loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a statement is to put it out or pronounce it, so the verb matches uttering words.

clue.text: Plant this dome on Eastern church

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bulb vegetable of the allium family
second meaning: the bulbous cupola typical of Russian Orthodox churches

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a dome on top of an Orthodox church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb telling you to place the dome; it is the noun, a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable gives its name to the bulb-shaped domes seen on Russian and other Eastern Orthodox churches.

indicators.note: something disgusting turns the stomach, hinting that the letters get turned over and rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to imitate a repulsive flatterer.
explanation.walkthrough: A toad-eater was a charlatan's assistant who pretended to eat toads; the word gave us 'toady', a fawning flatterer.
explanation.definitionFit: Toad-eater is the old word behind 'toady', a fawning flatterer, which is just what a sycophant is.

parts.note: surface reading: liquid measures arriving at the right moment
setter's reading: quarts are an example of measures, so these are measures of time

explanation.walkthrough: Quarts are just an example of a measure; a measurer of time is an accurate clock, its Greek roots chrono- and -meter meaning time and measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronometer is a precision timekeeper, literally a time-measurer, so it measures time as a quart measures liquid.

parts.note: to black goods is to boycott them, as unions did
a supporter of Britain joining the Common Market, the EEC

explanation.surface: A shady dealer complains about a prohibition imposed by a Brussels official.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiv is British slang for a flashy petty crook dealing in rationed goods; a Marketeer backed membership of the European Economic Community.
explanation.definitionFit: Spivs were wartime and postwar dealers in illicit or scarce goods, exactly the trade of an illegal market trader.

clue.text: Superior person in fancy linen, with gravity, is uplifting

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the next piece is added on
one thing placed in another sits within it
something fancy is elaborately done, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
a nob is a toff, someone of high social rank
the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A toff dressed in elegant linen, looking serious, is an inspiring sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Nob is British slang for an upper-class person; 'gravity' looks like solemnity but supplies its physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennobling means raising someone in dignity or character, so it is elevating or uplifting.

clue.text: Called about security cutting people off

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the next

parts.note: past tense of bid, to summon or call
a fastening that keeps things secure

explanation.surface: Someone phoned about a security measure isolating people.
explanation.walkthrough: BADE is the old past tense of bid, as in 'bade him enter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockade seals off a place so that its people are isolated from supplies and contact with the outside.

clue.text: Being charitable sort head shows mercy

parts.note: kind and affectionate
a sort or type
a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A generous sort of leader shows compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: A ness is a headland, a word surviving in British place names; 'head' here is land jutting into the sea, not a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Loving-kindness is tender compassion, the old Biblical term for God's merciful love toward people.

parts.note: the vanguard, the leading position
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sample of lead is found everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' sounds like the metal; it is the front, the van.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is a common flavour, the taste from orchid pods used in ice cream and baking.

clue.text: Flier one duped in the main?

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open ocean
a gull is a dupe, someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: A pilot asks if somebody was tricked on the high seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' sounds like 'mostly'; here the main is the sea, and the bird lives by it.
explanation.definitionFit: A seagull is a coastal bird, and any bird is a flier.

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the next word is read backwards
doing something wildly means doing it in disorder, so the word is jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A question about dashing madly round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: to career is to rush wildly about.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to move swiftly and uncontrollably, hurtling about at speed in a headlong rush.

clue.text: Puzzle of firm religious woman on rap

parts.note: short for company
a member of a female religious order
to drum is to tap or rap repeatedly

explanation.surface: A mystery about a company's nun performing rap music.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a riddle or a baffling problem, so it is another word for a puzzle.

parts.note: standard abbreviation for national
taken as written
standard abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A citizen has supported the Liberal party all his life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From birth' is an adjectival phrase, as in 'congenital', which is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal relates to birth, describing what belongs to a person by birth, as in a natal defect.

indicators.note: one item sitting in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: the initials of the learned society
pale and weak

explanation.surface: An academic headmaster swoons at a learned institution.
explanation.walkthrough: Bwana is the Swahili form of address meaning master or sir, used in colonial East Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: In Swahili the word is a respectful title for a man in authority, equivalent to sir or boss.

wordplay.note: with no Gospels, which are New Testament books, the Bible would be all Old Testament

explanation.surface: A cleric is told to hand out no Gospel readings.
explanation.walkthrough: The four Gospels open the New Testament, so a Bible without them leaves only the Old Testament, abbreviated OT.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or allocate a share, the same as assigning portions to people.

clue.text: Accessory put down to property's quality

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to credit something to a cause
second meaning: a noun, a characteristic feature

explanation.surface: Something extra on a building is blamed on what makes the property special.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue packs in senses of one word: an accessory symbol (a saint's emblem), the verb to ascribe, and a property or quality. Stress shifts between noun and verb.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means ascribe a cause; as a noun it names an inherent trait or characteristic of something.

parts.note: alternating current
standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Now is the moment to go on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current time' reads as 'the present'; it is two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to perform, either on stage or in carrying out a deed.

clue.text: Uniform embellishment of letter writer in letter from the East

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it
in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: the spelt-out name of the letter T
Saint Paul, author of many New Testament epistles

explanation.surface: A decoration on a uniform, sent by a correspondent in a letter from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'letter's look alike but do different jobs: PAUL wrote epistles, while TEE is the letter T, reversed to EET to house him.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulet is the ornamental shoulder piece on a military uniform, a decorative embellishment to it.

clue.text: Standard gruel served up on arrival

indicators.note: food served up is dished out and stirred about, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
short for arrival, as on timetables

explanation.surface: Ordinary porridge is dished out to newcomers when they arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular and standard both describe something normal, usual, or conforming to an accepted pattern.
